title: Solar Heat Transfer & Hydration Station
description: Simulate a desert scene where a ShadowmappableMesh acts as a terrain surface absorbing solar heat, sunglasses filter UV intensity, and a water bottle serves as a coolant reservoir. The user manipulates sun angle, UV filter level via sunglasses positioning, and water dispensing to maintain thermal equilibrium across terrain zones while obeying energy conservation laws.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader from CDN. Load ShadowmappableMesh.glb as a terrain platform at the scene center, SunglassesKhronos.glb floating above-left as a UV filter device, and WaterBottle.glb above-right as a coolant dispenser. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0,5,10) with OrbitControls. Add a DirectionalLight as the sun with shadow mapping enabled on the terrain mesh. Divide the terrain conceptually into a 3x3 grid of heat zones, each with a temperature value starting at 50°C displayed via colored overlays (blue=cold, red=hot). Implement these interactions: (1) A sun-angle slider (0-180°) rotates the DirectionalLight around the scene, redistributing heat — zones in shadow cool, zones in light heat up. (2) Clicking the sunglasses model toggles through 3 UV filter levels (none, partial, full) which scale the heating rate globally by 1.0, 0.5, 0.2 respectively — animate the sunglasses tint opacity to reflect this. (3) Clicking the water bottle then clicking a terrain zone dispenses 10 units of coolant, reducing that zone's temperature by 15°C. The bottle holds 50 total coolant units displayed as a fill-level bar. (4) Enforce energy conservation: total system energy is constant — cooling one zone redistributes heat to adjacent zones. (5) Implement undo/redo buttons that track all state changes (sun angle, filter level, water dispensing) in a history stack supporting at least 14 steps. (6) Add a HUD showing each zone's temperature, coolant remaining, current filter level, sun angle, and total system energy. (7) A reset button restores initial state. (8) Zones reaching 100°C flash red and trigger a warning. The goal is to bring all 9 zones within 40-60°C simultaneously. Display a success banner when achieved. Use smooth animations for all transitions.
